title: LL4-050: full four-input flat levels with binary remainder recovery, lower classical memory at source coefficient1/2

claims.statement: For every N>=2 and s in Z/NZ, with n=ceil(log2 N), the single LL4-050 algorithm and full configuration of proof.md (finite branch n<2^32; otherwise r=ceil(sqrt n), z=ceil(log2 r), m=floor(r/4)-10z, lambda=ceil(4r/3)+200z, kappa=ceil(log2(m+3))+3, u full four-input flat levels with exact width3lambda-kappa, three binary finishing levels with exact remainder allocation, all hard counters, free-frequency odd decoder and controlled-shift 2-adic recovery) outputs the full secret with unconditional probability at least1-2^-8>2/3 from independent ideal copies. On EVERY branch including retries, failures, discarded copies and aborts, total charged sequential work is T(N,s)=O(n^(389/2)2^((19/6)sqrt n)). The exact uniform envelope B_T(n)=n^(389/2)2^((19/6)sqrt n) has growth index1/2 and an absolute outside constant. The ledger includes fiber enumeration, all source/extraction costs, classical processing, lookup/circuit generation, decoding, initialization, reset, measurement and addressing. This holds jointly with the other three resource bounds and zero-tolerance claim for the same algorithm/configuration.

For the same LL4-050 algorithm/configuration of proof.md, for every N>=2 and s, n=ceil(log2 N), peak classical allocation on EVERY branch is S_C(N,s)=O(n^(203/2)2^((4/3)sqrt n)) bits, including the depth-first full-label tables, bounded four-input fiber lists, heaps, buffers, extraction scratch and decoder records. The exact uniform envelope B_C(n)=n^(203/2)2^((4/3)sqrt n) has growth index1/2 and an absolute outside constant. This holds jointly with unconditional full-secret success at least1-2^-8 and all the other resource and zero-tolerance claims for this same configuration.

For the same LL4-050 algorithm and configuration of proof.md, for every N >= 2 and every s in Z/NZ, with n = ceil(log2 N), peak quantum memory on every execution branch is S_Q(N,s) = O(n) qubits, with an absolute constant, including the depth-first index registers and all ancillas. The envelope B_Q(n) = n has growth index exactly 0. This holds jointly with the stated work, classical-memory and sample bounds and full-secret success probability at least 1 - 2^-8.

For the same LL4-050 algorithm and configuration of proof.md, for every N >= 2 and every s in Z/NZ, with n = ceil(log2 N), the total number Q(N,s) of fresh DCP source copies acquired on every execution branch, including every discarded copy and every failed or aborted attempt, is O(2^((1/2) sqrt n)), with an absolute constant. The stronger main-branch bound is Q <= n Ccap + K = O(n^3 r^(-20) 2^(r/2)), with Ccap and K defined in proof.md. The uniform bit-length envelope B_samples(n) = 2^((1/2) sqrt n) has growth index exactly 1/2. This holds jointly with the stated work and memory bounds and unconditional full-secret success probability at least 1 - 2^-8.

For the same LL4-050 algorithm and configuration of proof.md, the proved fractional error tolerance is epsilon(n) = 0: all Q source copies are independent ideal coset states. Under this promise, for every N and s, full-secret recovery succeeds with probability at least 1 - 2^-8 jointly with all four resource bounds. No positive corruption tolerance is asserted; this is not a proof that greater tolerance is impossible.

structured.error_model: Malformed fraction among acquired copies. The proved guarantee requires every copy to be an independent ideal coset state; no behavior is promised for malformed copies.
